title: Microsoft Tech Support Scam
description: Do these warnings, pop-ups and alerts look familiar? If so, cyber criminals may be trying to destroy you, or at least you take over your computer.   In honor of National Cyber Security month, today we are talking about tech support scams, also known as the Microsoft support scam.   An ad shows up on your computer, “YOUR COMPUTER IS INFECTED. YOUR PERSONAL AND FINANCIAL INFORMATION IS NOT SAFE. TO REMOVE VIRUSES, CALL TECH SUPPORT IMMEDIATELY”  People are falling victim to this scam every day by giving their money, and personal information to complete strangers.  And just when you think it won’t happen to you - it does.   Here’s three ways you can protect yourself, and your precious PC from Microsoft Support Scams.  1. Don’t click on the Pop-Up alerts, and definitely don’t call the number on the screen.  Don’t even click on the X to close the pop-ups, because when you do, it will only create additional pop-ups. Instead, try using your task manager to close the program by hitting CTRL + ALT + DELETE.   2. Never give remote access to your computer.  Remote access means someone in a different location controls your PC. Instead, take it to a tech support business with a physical location. For a list of Accredited tech repair companies go to bbb.org.   3. Keep your anti-virus and anti-spyware software updated & use a good firewall.  Remember if you need help with this, find a list of trustworthy businesses at bbb.org.   If you’ve already fallen victim to one of these scams and you need tips on how to recover, click the link in the top-right corner of this video.  If you need help, or want to report a scam, contact your local Better Business Bureau at bbb.org or leave a comment on this video!

asr.full_text: Do these warnings, pop-ups, and alerts look familiar? If so, cyber criminals may be trying to destroy you. Hey guys, I'm Danielle from the Sacramento Better Business Bureau, and this is Torch Talk. In honor of National Cybersecurity Month, today we're talking about tech support scams, also known as the Microsoft support scam. An ad shows up on your computer. Your computer is infected. Your personal and financial information is not safe. To remove viruses, call tech support immediately. People are falling victim to this scam every day by giving their money or personal information to complete strangers. And just when you think it won't happen to you, it does. Here are three ways you can protect yourself and your precious PC from Microsoft support scams. Don't click on the pop-up alerts and definitely don't call the number on the screen. Don't even click on the X to close the pop-up, because when you do, it'll only create more pop-ups. Instead, try using your task manager to close the program by hitting Control-Alt-Delete. Do not give remote access to your computer unless you're absolutely sure you know who you're talking to. Remote access means someone in a different location controls your PC. Instead, take it to a tech support business with a physical location. For a list of accredited tech repair companies, go to BBB.org. Keep your antivirus and anti-spyware software updated and use a good firewall. Remember, if you need help on this, find a list of trustworthy businesses at BBB.org. If you think you've already fallen victim to one of these scams, click on the link in the top right corner of this video. If you need help or want to report a scam, contact your local Better Business Bureau at BBB.org. I'm Danielle, thanks for watching. Please subscribe for the latest Torch Talk.
